A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–F. All 32 pages of each version support comparison; the scientific content matches throughout.

before.justification: v2 reports original unlearning experiments on CIFAR-10 and IMDb in Section 5, Figures 2–4 and Table 1, plus supplementary experiments and regression analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main unlearning comparisons, appendix sensitivity analyses and regression experiments investigating unlearning failure.

M1.justification: The Gaussian poisoning method, input-gradient evaluation statistic and four-step evaluation procedure in Section 4 are unchanged. Algorithms 1–4 and the unlearning procedures in Appendix D also match.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10 image classification, IMDb sentiment analysis and the regression settings in Appendix F. The Gaussian, targeted, backdoor and indiscriminate poisoning scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated methods remain GD, NGD, GA, EUk, CFk, SCRUB, NegGrad+ (NGP) and SSD, with identical membership within corresponding experiments. Retraining controls and standard membership-inference comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: Section 5 and the appendices retain the same models, training budgets, poison budgets, metrics and testing procedures. These include ResNet-18 training for 100 epochs, GPT-2 fine-tuning for 10 epochs and unlearning budgets up to 10% of original training compute.

E4.justification: The input-dimensionality analysis, SSD hyperparameter sweep, update-step and forget-set sensitivity studies, targeted-attack brittleness analysis and model-shift investigations are all retained without revision in Appendices B, E and F.

E5.justification: Both versions state that vision and language results typically average eight and five runs, respectively, usually reporting ±1 standard deviation. Appendix F.2 also retains five poison initializations and five random subsets. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, at 10 epochs and 1.5% poisoning, Table 1 reports 87.71% accuracy for GD and 89.24% for retraining in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Gaussian hypothesis-testing formulation and dimension-dependent tradeoff derivation in Appendix B are unchanged. The attack objectives and unlearning equations in Appendix D also match.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about unlearning failures, task-dependent effectiveness, Gaussian poisoning as an evaluation method and two hypotheses explaining failure. No contribution is added, removed or strengthened.

C2.justification: The explanations involving larger model shifts and orthogonal update directions in Section 6 are unchanged. Task-dependent interpretations and qualifications, including the potentially unrealistic unbounded perturbations in Appendix D.1.3, are also retained.

D1.justification: Implementation instructions, hyperparameters, runtime information and synthetic-data construction details remain unchanged. Both versions provide the same OpenUnlearn code-access statement and the same technical disclosures in the appendices.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A and the references contain the same cited works and research positioning. Comparisons with prior membership-inference evaluations and poisoning-based unlearning studies are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 places Gautam Kamath before Ayush Sekhari, identifies Kamath, Sekhari and Seth Neel as equal advisory contributors, and adds Harvard to Neel's affiliations. The scientific prose, section order and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Minor visual edits affect the first-page byline, contribution footnote and arXiv margin stamp. Figures 1–14 and Tables 1–5 retain their displays, captions, axes and placement; the remaining page organization is unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 updates contributor attribution and affiliations while preserving the methods, empirical evidence, mathematical analysis, interpretations and appendices. These limited administrative and presentation edits do not materially improve or weaken the paper's overall quality.
